intro: The Pythagorean theorem relates a right triangle's legs and hypotenuse: $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Common triples are $3$-$4$-$5$ and $5$-$12$-$13$. Special right triangles: a $45$-$45$-$90$ has sides $x,x,x\sqrt{2}$; a $30$-$60$-$90$ has sides $x,x\sqrt{3},2x$. Right-triangle trig uses SOH-CAH-TOA: $\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}$, $\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}$, $\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$. Also, $\sin\theta=\cos(90^\circ-\theta)$.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs $3$ and $4$. Find the hypotenuse.
In a right triangle, the side opposite $\theta$ is $3$ and the hypotenuse is $5$. Find $\sin\theta$.
In a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle, each leg is $4$. Find the hypotenuse.
Longer leg of $30$-$60$-$90$ with short leg $5$.
